Congress wants Akhilesh as UP CM but seeks ‘more space’ in seat-sharing deal: Imran Masood
Masood has accused the SP of belittling the party by offering only 26 seats in UP, despite Mallikarjun Kharge urging him to focus more on action than words.
Amid the ongoing SP-Congress seat-sharing tussle in Uttar Pradesh, Congress leader Imran Masood set the record straight, saying the party wanted Akhilesh Yadav as the next chief minister, but needed "more space" in the seat-sharing arrangement.
His remarks came after the Samajwadi Party offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of discussions, while the latter has reportedly asked for over 100 seats. The SP also rolled out its first list of five candidates, covering constituencies in Saharanpur, Shamli, Amroha, and Lalitpur.
Masood, the Congress's state working president, has openly called for an "adequate number of seats", accusing the SP of belittling the party despite party president Mallikarjun Kharge pulling him up for focusing more on words than action.
Deep Dive
"Our position is very clear. We want the elections to be fought together, and we want Akhilesh Yadav to become the UP CM. But our only demand is that we too should be given space," he told news agency PTI, saying Yadav "should show generosity".
Masood further stressed that the Congress cannot enter the elections by "surrendering itself". He also repeated his "beggar" remark in response to SP leader Azam Khan asking Masood to maintain restraint in seat-sharing negotiations.
"We are not beggars asking you for something. We have nothing to ask from you. That is all I will say on this," he added.
Masood accuses SP of "belittling" Congress
This came after Masood accused the SP of "belittling an ally" on Friday, saying that the Congress wanted both "quality and quantity" to fight the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the upcoming elections.

"Give us seats, we can contest and win. We need both quality and quantity... You [SP] take the chief minister's post. There is no dispute here regarding the chief minister. But why are you trying to undermine your ally? Why do you want to belittle your ally?" he was quoted as saying by the BJP.
Masood has been vocal in his criticism of the SP after it released its first list of five candidates for next year's Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, which included two seats in Saharanpur, where Masood is the sitting MP.
He said the Congress will accept a seat-sharing arrangement with the SP only if it is "respectable and acceptable" and also hinted at other political options if the talks failed to materialise.
Kharge's message to Masood
His remarks came a day after Mallikarjun Kharge visited the Uttar Pradesh capital on Constitution Day, where the Congress president made clear that the alliance between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress was aimed at thwarting the BJP.
Kharge urged the outspoken UP Congress leader to focus on action rather than making statements. "Imran Masood ji puts forward his views with great enthusiasm. I also hear him regularly on television, where he speaks quite forcefully. But more than statements, we have to work on the ground," he said in Lucknow.
Asked to comment on Kharge's advice for him, Masood said, "Kharge sahib has praised me. I am also saying that the alliance is there.
Also Read | Day after Kharge rebuke, Masood says Congress wants over 105 seats in UP polls
Congress-SP seat-sharing row
Akhilesh Yadav had recently revealed at the HT Leadership Summit that the Congress had sought 181 seats during the initial round of discussions, adding that a seat-sharing arrangement could be worked out on the basis of the winnability of candidates.
However, reports surfaced that the Congress has asked for 110-120 seats in the ongoing seat-sharing talks after the SP offered 26 seats in the initial round of negotiations. Masood's displeasure at being offered 26 seats has triggered a sharp reaction from the SP, urging the party to focus on seats it can actually win so the partners can resolve differences quickly.
The Congress and SP have been allies in the past. In the 2017 assembly elections, they contested together, with the Congress fighting 114 seats and winning seven, while the SP won 47. The BJP won 312 seats and formed the government. The Congress contested the 2022 assembly elections on its own and won only two seats.

Maharashtra warns schools of action for barring ST students from exams over pending scholarship dues
The government said the students cannot be penalised for delays in the disbursement of funds by the state.
The Maharashtra government has warned schools and educational institutions of administrative action if they prevent Scheduled Tribe (ST) students from appearing for examinations or withhold their academic documents over pending scholarship and fee reimbursement dues.
The state government has said that institutional heads will be held accountable for such violations, and that students cannot be penalised for delays in the disbursement of funds by the state.
A circular to this effect was issued by the state school education department on Friday. It prohibited institutions from denying eligible ST students access to entrance examinations, state board examinations or any other academic examination on the grounds that their scholarship or fee reimbursement claims are pending.
The directives were issued in the wake of complaints that educational institutions have been demanding fees from students despite their eligibility for government reimbursement. In some cases, students have been barred from examinations or had their academic documents withheld because of non-payment.
The state government provides scholarships to students from the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community to help them pursue higher education. However, students have complained that delays in the release of scholarship funds have led to harassment by various means.
Against this backdrop, the circular explicitly states that institutions cannot create hurdles in the submission of examination forms, issuance of hall tickets or participation in any other academic process.
"The schools have been prohibited from withholding Leaving Certificates, mark sheets, bonafide certificates, result sheets or any other academic documents because scholarship or fee reimbursement payments have not been received," the circular said.
Further, institutions have been directed not to demand advance payment of fees eligible for reimbursement under the relevant government schemes or deprive students of educational facilities on that account.
The circular makes institutional heads directly accountable for violations. "If an institution is found preventing students from appearing for examinations, withholding their academic documents or taking any other action that causes academic loss, its head will be held responsible and appropriate administrative action will be initiated under the applicable acts, rules and government resolutions," the circular noted.
The directive will apply to all educational institutions under the school education department, including government-run schools, institutions managed by local self-government bodies, aided schools and recognised self-financed institutions.
All education officers, divisional deputy directors and other administrative officials have been instructed to bring the circular to the notice of institutions under their jurisdiction and ensure its strict implementation.
The state government has also ensured that students' complaints in this regard are addressed promptly, and has introduced a time-bound grievance redressal mechanism. At the institutional level, the headmaster or principal will have to resolve complaints within three working days. At the taluka and district levels, the education officer (primary/secondary) will have seven working days, while the divisional deputy director of education will have the same timeframe.
At the state level, the Director of Education (Primary or Secondary) will be required to intervene immediately, wherever necessary.

morning.text:
CRPF personnel deployed in Tamil Nadu's Tirupparankundram ahead of Deepathoon lamp lighting
CRPF personnel reached Tirupparankundram hill near Madurai after the Supreme Court directed that the lamp be lit at the disputed Deepathoon stone pillar.
Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel arrived at Tirupparankundram hill near Madurai in Tamil Nadu early on Saturday ahead of the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon (stone pillar), following a Supreme Court directive to provide security for the event.
A company of CRPF personnel, normally comprising 100 to 135 personnel, arrived at the hill in the early hours of Saturday to maintain security, a senior commander said.
“A company of CRPF personnel arrived here today. I cannot say anything more than this,” the commander told reporters, declining to answer further questions.
Deep Dive
Meanwhile, workers were seen carrying wooden logs to erect a temporary structure around the Deepathoon as preparations for lighting the lamp atop the hill continued. The sthanika bhattars (hereditary priests), as directed by the Supreme Court, will decide the time at which the lamp is to be lit.
Preparations underway for Deepathoon lamp lighting
On November 24, coinciding with the Karthigai Deepam festival in Tamil Nadu, the ceremonial lamp at the Deepam Mandapam near the Uchi Pillayar Temple was lit at 6pm by the temple board’s trustees. It was not immediately clear whether the lamp at the Deepathoon would also be lit at 6pm on Saturday.
On Friday, the Supreme Court directed that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon and ordered the deployment of CRPF personnel to maintain security instead of the local police.
SC appoints former judges as temple receivers
The court also suspended the existing members of the Board of Trustees that administers the Arulmigu Subramanya Swamy Temple at Tirupparankundram and appointed former judges S Vaidyanathan and V Parthipan as receivers to manage the temple. The temple also administers the Uchi Pillayar Temple, and its Board of Trustees functions under the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department.
The Supreme Court directed that the flame used to light the Deepathoon be taken from the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillayar Temple, where the lamp was lit by the Tamil Nadu government on November 24 in accordance with the
Deepathoon lamp lighting dispute
The dispute over the Deepathoon intensified in 2025 after members of Hindu outfits demanded that the ceremonial lamp be lit at the stone pillar, located about 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah. For decades, the lamp had been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillayar Temple on the lower slopes of the hill.
On Saturday, around 200 members of Muslim groups climbed the hill, also known as Sikandar Hill, to offer prayers at the dargah amid tight security. The hill is also referred to as Sikandar Hill because it houses the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.
The row escalated after the temple board failed to comply with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order permitting the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the stone pillar.
In a status report submitted on Wednesday, Madurai collector Nishant Krishna apologised to the Supreme Court for not lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon but placed responsibility for the decision on the temple board.
Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu’s survey and archaeology departments have identified the disputed stone pillar as a Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) marker, reiterating the state’s argument before the Supreme Court against lighting the Karthigai Deepam there.
The report, titled Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) Stations in Tamil Nadu, prepared by the Department of Survey and Settlement and the Department of Archaeology, examines the historical and geographical significance of survey markers. It identifies the pillar at Sikandarmalai, another name for Tirupparankundram hill, as a British-era GTS station.

morning.text:
Supreme Court extends bail of two accused in 2020 Delhi riots case by three months
Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi face charges under UAPA in the 2020 Delhi riots case. Their interim bail has been extended until February 2027.
The Supreme Court has extended the interim bail granted to two accused in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case, Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, by three months, giving them relief from having to surrender as the larger bench considers the legal position on bail under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).
A bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi granted the extension to Ahmed on Friday. Saifi was granted similar relief by the same bench on November 25. The two had approached the court seeking an extension of the six-month interim bail granted to them on May 22. The period was due to expire on November 25, after which they would have had to surrender.
“The application is allowed and interim bail granted earlier stands extended by three months with effect from November 25, 2026,” the court said in its order on Friday.
Both are facing charges under the UAPA in the conspiracy case linked to the Delhi riots.
On May 22, while granting them interim bail, the Supreme Court had observed that the issue of granting bail under the UAPA required consideration by a larger bench in view of a contrary ruling by another bench of the top court on whether delay in trial could be a ground for granting bail.
In their applications, Ahmed and Saifi said that they had been released from jail on May 25 and that their six-month interim bail period had expired, while the larger bench was yet to be constituted. In September 2025, the Delhi high court had rejected their bail pleas, prompting them to approach the Supreme Court.
The trial in the Delhi riots conspiracy case involves 18 accused. Of these, five — Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmed — were granted bail by the Supreme Court on January 5. In the same order, the court rejected the bail pleas of former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and student activist Sharjeel Imam.
Ahmed and Saifi had relied on the January 5 order to seek bail. However, while considering their pleas, the Delhi Police drew the court’s attention to a May 18 order passed by another Supreme Court bench, which had expressed reservations about the January 5 ruling denying bail to Khalid and Imam.
The bench hearing Ahmed and Saifi’s pleas referred to the May 18 judgment in the case of Syed Iftikhar Andrabi, an accused in a separate UAPA case. It directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India (CJI) to reconcile the two rulings on the interpretation of Section 43D(5) of the UAPA. The provision imposes stringent restrictions on bail, requiring courts to assess whether the allegations against an accused are prima facie true before granting relief.
The May 18 judgment had expressed reservations about the January 5 ruling, stating: “We have serious reservations on various aspects of the judgment...including foreclosing the right of the two appellants [Khalid and Imam] to seek bail for a period of one year.”
It also questioned the January 5 judgment’s interpretation of a 2021 three-judge bench ruling in the KA Najeeb case, which had deprecated prolonged pre-trial detention. The Andrabi judgment held that the three-judge bench ruling was binding on all courts, including benches of lesser strength in the Supreme Court.
Khalid and Imam have since filed separate petitions seeking bail. The Supreme Court admitted their pleas this week and issued notice to the Delhi Police, seeking its response. Their petitions are scheduled to be heard by a three-judge bench on December 14, along with the main matter concerning the interpretation of bail provisions under the UAPA.

Keralam govt approves ₹40 lakh for informant, police rewards under 'Operation Toofan'
Thiruvananthapuram, The Keralam government has approved ₹40 lakh for rewarding police teams and covert informants involved in its statewide anti-narcotics campaign, Operation Toofan, officials said on Saturday.
Recently, the State Police Chief requested the state government to provide ₹2.74 crore for investigation, prosecution and incentive-related expenses as part of the 'Operation Toofan'.
According to a Home Department order issued on November 24, ₹2.34 crore has been sanctioned for investigation and prosecution expenses, particularly for tracing and arresting sources involved in narcotics cases.
The remaining ₹40 lakh has been allocated for rewards to police teams and covert sources or informants involved in the campaign.
The order stipulates that there should be no duplication of rewards under any other scheme and directs the State Police Chief to ensure that informants are rewarded on par with police teams.
The latest allocation is part of the ₹10 crore administrative sanction earlier accorded by the government for the implementation of Operation Toofan – The Narco Hunt.
As of November 26, the anti-drug drive has resulted in the arrest of 17,424 people and the registration of 16,117 cases across the state so far, according to the latest Kerala Police figures.
The data shared by the police said that it has seized 30.826 kg of MDMA, 2,110.462 kg of ganja and 8.261 kg of hashish oil as part of the operation.
As many as 55 people were arrested in 50 cases, with seizures including 18.910 grams of MDMA, 12.784 kg of ganja and 2.02 grams of hashish oil on November 26 alone,
The police have also conducted 12,626 awareness classes as part of the campaign, officials said.
At the same time, school and college protection groups have organised 8,664 awareness programmes after Operation Toofan was launched in June this year.
The public can share information about drug trafficking with the police through phone numbers 9497979794 and 9497927797 or WhatsApp number 9995966666.
The identity of informants will be kept confidential, the police said.

UP may have 605 MLAs after delimitation, only state to cross 600-mark
The proposed 132nd constitutional amendment bill caps the ceiling to 650 seats in legislative assemblies.
The proposed 132nd Constitution amendment bill paves the way for a 50% increase in the strength of all state and Union territory assemblies, while capping the maximum number of seats at 650. Uttar Pradesh's Assembly could have 605 MLAs after 2029.
The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, circulated among parliamentarians on Friday, lays down the details of the country's proposed electoral map, which could undergo a major expansion in three years.
While the legislation amends Article 334 to increase the strength of all legislative bodies by 50%, it also amends Article 170 to cap the maximum number of seats in state assemblies at 650.
This means that while all other states will see a 50% increase in their Assembly strength, Uttar Pradesh, which currently has 403 seats, will have 605 MLAs after 2029, making it the only state with more than 600 legislators.
The state will also have 120 Lok Sabha MPs after the delimitation exercise.
State numbers to balloon
The 294-member West Bengal Assembly will expand to 441 seats, while Maharashtra's 288-member Assembly will increase to 432 seats.
The Bill states: "In Article 170 of the Constitution,–– (a) in clause (1), for the words “five hundred”, the words “six hundred and fifty” shall be substituted.”
Article 170 currently caps the strength of state assemblies at 500 seats, with Uttar Pradesh having the highest number of seats at 403.
Two senior parliamentary officials told HT that most state assemblies would require new buildings, as their existing chambers do not have enough space to accommodate the additional legislators.
The Uttar Pradesh Assembly building, inaugurated in 1928, and the West Bengal Assembly building, inaugurated in 1931, may not have sufficient space to accommodate the expanded strength after 2029, officials said.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri in another case after a packaged drinking water sample collected from its West Bengal plant failed laboratory testing, according to news agency PTI.

The move has cost the state over ₹2.20 crore. Officials say the expenditure could be recovered through savings on paper, printing and manual file handling
The Bihar government has decided to go paperless, with the latest models of iPads issued to the chief minister, deputy chief ministers, all ministers, the chief secretary, the additional chief secretary (cabinet), secretaries to the CM and a handful of other key officers for official work.
Chief minister Samrat Choudhary also chaired the first paperless meeting of the council of ministers in Patna on Wednesday.

The move has cost the state over ₹2.20 crore, with officials saying the expenditure could be recovered through savings on paper, printing and manual file handling, possibly within six to seven months. The system is designed to speed up the circulation of urgent proposals and reduce the physical movement of bulky agendas.
e-cabinet system rolled out after weeks of trials
The software, developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC), runs on authorised iPads managed by the cabinet secretariat department. Following around one-and-a-half months of trial runs and training sessions for ministers and officials, the platform was activated at the latest cabinet meeting. The same application, with limited features, can also be accessed on designated laptops running Android, additional chief secretary (cabinet) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary said.
A senior cabinet secretariat officer noted that ministers already receive advanced laptops from their respective departments. However, a senior cabinet minister said most ministers rarely operate these devices themselves, with personal assistants handling the iPads and laptops in practice, despite the training sessions organised by the department.
Files and iPads to coexist for now
For now, the old and new systems will operate side by side. Hard copies of agendas will continue to be distributed for the next few weeks before physical files are phased out completely.
“Both systems of the cabinet meeting, physical as well as e-cabinet, will run concurrently for the next few weeks before finally discontinuing the presentation of hard copies,” the ACS said.

Bihar has become the 12th state to shift cabinet proceedings online. The first e-cabinet meeting cleared 34 proposals, including a major administrative sanction for the Patna water supply project under AMRUT 2.0.
The digital push in the executive comes against the backdrop of similar changes already under way in the legislature. Under the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA), tablets have been installed on the desks of members in both Houses. The Bihar Legislative Council was among the early adopters, with devices installed at every member's seat several years ago.
In the Assembly, tablets have also been installed as part of the paperless push, including at the desks of ministers who are members of the House. However, a nodal officer of the Assembly clarified that ministers were not given additional personal devices beyond those provided during the initial phase of the Council's digital rollout.
The e-cabinet is the latest addition to Bihar's gradual shift towards digital governance. Whether the gadgets become tools of greater efficiency or remain largely in the hands of personal staff will become clearer in the weeks ahead, as the paper-based and digital systems continue to operate in parallel.

Ridhima Gupta is a Principal Correspondent at Hindustan Times, where she covers healthcare, pharmaceuticals, and public health policy. Her reporting centers on Delhi’s major hospitals (AIIMS, Safdarjung, Lok Nayak), the state health department, and emerging medical trends. Ridhima is particularly interested in reporting on healthcare issues through the lens of women, children, and persons with disabilities. Her work often explores the intersection of healthcare and public policy, examining how these factors shape access health care. Based in New Delhi, many of her reports have led to direct government action over the years, in different city. Earlier this year, she completed a media training workshop on the Impact of Extreme Heat on Health, organised by the Global Strategic Communications Council (GSCC), further strengthening her interest in reporting on the intersection of climate change and public health. A postgraduate from the Asian College of Journalism, Chennai, Ridhima has around a decade of experience in journalism. She began her career as a trainee television reporter with Mirror Now in Mumbai and has since worked across multiple cities, including Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Delhi, contributing to both print and broadcast newsrooms. She is a recipient of the Laadli Media Fellowship (2022) for her reporting on education, disability, and women’s issues. Before joining Hindustan Times, Ridhima worked with The Times of India, New Indian Express and News18. A native of Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, Ridhima completed her undergraduate studies in Biotechnology. And when she is not working as a journalist she likes to paint and go on nature hikes.
Safdarjung Hospital denies hiring fake doctor accused of using forged MBBS, MD degrees
SOG additional director general Vishal Bansal told HT that investigators had also found a photograph of Mahawar in a Safdarjung staff uniform on his phone.
Safdarjung Hospital on Friday denied that Ramkishor Mahawar, who had not passed Class 11 and has been arrested in an interstate fake medical degree racket, ever worked there. The Rajasthan Police’s special operations group (SOG), which had on Thursday said he was a contractual junior resident at the hospital, said Mahawar had told officials during interrogation that he worked at the Delhi hospital.
“As per the official records of the hospital, the individual named in the report has never worked at Safdarjung hospital, including on a contractual basis,” the Vardhman Mahavir Medical College (VMMC) and Safdarjung Hospital said in a statement on Friday.
It said it follows prescribed rules and procedures, and exercises “due vigilance” when hiring staff and verifying their credentials.

SOG additional director general Vishal Bansal told HT that investigators had also found a photograph of Mahawar in a Safdarjung staff uniform on his mobile phone. ‘The interrogation is still ongoing. More important revelations are expected. Safdarjung Hospital will be contacted after this,’ he said.”
Mahawar's documents
The SOG said on Thursday that Mahawar claimed to have had joined Safdarjung in June 2025 after registering with the Delhi Medical Council (DMC) on forged MBBS and MD degrees. The DMC has since told the SOG, in a letter seen by HT, that it never registered him and did not issue the registration certificate he held. That certificate is dated July 10, 2025, a month after the date the SOG gives for his purported joining Safdarjung.
Documents obtained by HT show that Mahawar presented himself as a senior specialist at several places in Delhi. A visiting card for a clinic in Janakpuri describes him as a senior consultant in obstetrics and gynaecology, a foetal medicine specialist and a laparoscopy surgeon.
It also says he was a senior consultant at a private hospital in central Delhi and at a hospital in Najafgarh.
The card lists an MD from King George’s Medical University (KGMU), Lucknow, and fellowships in foetal and reproductive medicine from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi.
The clinic’s address on the card is the same as the home address on his forged DMC certificate.
Police have said Mahawar worked as a nursing assistant, or ward boy, at a private hospital in Delhi between August 2024 and April 2025, and that he later used a fake diploma in medical radio diagnosis to take on-call sonography work at various Delhi hospitals.
The documents – all forged - also contradict one another. An admission letter purportedly issued by Government Medical College, Miraj, in Maharashtra, in June 2012 admits him to an MBBS course for 2012–17. A degree purportedly issued by Sikkim Manipal University in December 2017 says he qualified in 2016.
Past working records
A DMC certificate – the council said on Thursday it had not issued any registration to him - lists an MBBS from 2017 and an MD in obstetrics and gynaecology from 2022, both from Sikkim Manipal, and a diploma in medical radio diagnosis from the Miraj college in 2025.
The SOG has said that from 2016 to 2022 he was working at a private nursing home in Dausa, Rajasthan. HT could not independently verify the documents or his claimed links with the hospitals.
Mahawar, whose name appears as Ram Kishor and Ram Kishore in some documents, paid about ₹5.5 lakh for forged Class 11, MBBS and MD certificates, police said. He had also registered with the Rajasthan and Maharashtra medical councils.

The SOG arrested Mahawar in Delhi on November 8, and the three other accused, Satyajit Panigrahi, Manish Manjhi and Khurram Taufiq, in Mumbai, Gwalior and Azamgarh between November 18 and 24. Bansal has said the accused were in contact online and there was no single mastermind.
The SOG says the racket forged certificates of 45 to 55 universities and educational institutions, and that it is still looking for other buyers and members of the network.
The investigation began with a complaint that the Rajasthan Medical Council’s registrar filed in Jaipur in October 2024 about people who had registered as doctors with forged documents.

morning.text:
Hemendra Chaturvedi is a senior journalist based at Agra. He covers eight districts of Agra and Aligarh division namely Agra, Mathura, Mainpuri, Firozabad, Aligarh, Etah, Kasganj and Hathras. He had been with HT since 1992 and has completed three decades of association with HT and has worked for Hindustan Times only all through his career of about 35 years. Having Masters in Chemistry, Hemendra is also a law graduate with diploma in Personnel Management and has utilised broad based academic qualifications in his indepth, accurate and high impact stories from this part of western Uttar Pradesh while being based in the city of Taj Mahal. In such long span of career with Hindustan Times, Hemendra Chaturvedi has led his team of reporters which was instrumental in bringing out supplements including Region Scan, Agra Live, HT City time to time and proven his leadership qualities and has made presence of HT felt in the region covered by him. In the process of time, Hemendra has attained expertise in a variety of beats, being sole reporter for HT and has covered Aligarh Muslim University, Taj Mahal centric tourism, religiously sensitive city of Mathura and had been witness to Agra Summit having attendance of top leaders of India and Pakistan.
Taj’s neglected backyard may get new lease of green life as 40,000 square-metre garden takes shape
The plan follows Supreme Court-backed efforts to increase greenery in the Taj Trapezium Zone.
For two decades, a large stretch of the Yamuna bank between the Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal lay fallow, courtesy the much-hyped-but-eventually-shelved Taj heritage corridor project.
Now, that might change. The state horticulture department is turning a 40,000-square-metre patch of this land into a landscaped garden. Uttar Pradesh horticulture minister Dinesh Pratap Singh said the state decided to develop the land with two aims. “The first is to protect the Taj from dust and pollution by increasing green cover and planting more trees. The second is to give tourists a more serene and beautiful setting from which to view the monument. An initial amount of around ₹1.5 crore was allocated and work is likely to be completed in the next few months,” he added.
Rajnish Pandey, superintendent of the state horticulture department in Agra, said three lawns already existed in front of the Agra Fort. “There is another patch of land measuring 40,000 square metres alongside the river Yamuna, facing the Agra Fort, which was not in a good state and reflected the remains of the unfinished Taj heritage corridor project. It has now been taken up by the state horticulture department to be developed on the pattern of the three existing lawns,” Pandey told HT.
Also read: Taj Mahal security reviewed, blind spots identified
Existing trees to be preserved as ornamental and seasonal plants are added
When HT visited the site, about a dozen women workers were clearing pebbles and stones from the ground. Many trees had grown on the land over the years. Officials said these will be preserved and made part of the landscaping. “The area will be filled with ornamental plants besides seasonal ones to add natural beauty,” Pandey said.
The site lies along Yamuna Kinara Road, facing the Agra Fort and looking towards the Taj Mahal. It is part of a cluster of Taj View Gardens, landscaped lawns along the river from which visitors can view the Taj Mahal. Two belong to the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). The horticulture department has one garden of over 25,000 square metres.
In all, about 26-29 acres of land between the two monuments is being developed. Of this, ASI has about 10-12 acres, while the horticulture department has about 16-17 acres, including its existing garden and the new patch. Work on the project began in September. “We might have some cultural events after due permission if things go as planned. It will provide green cover much needed to hold SPM (suspended particulate matter) in the air around the Taj Mahal,” said Pandey.
Agra Development Authority vice-chairperson Vijay Kumar said the body was backing the project at every stage.
Also read: Green patches re-appear on Taj Mahal walls, ASI on alert
Supreme Court directions underpin efforts to increase green cover near Taj
An ASI official said the agency had its own green landscape. “Our gardens are spread over an area of about 10 to 12 acres and are towards the river Yamuna” he said. “These green landscapes are coming up in compliance with directions of the Supreme Court in the matter related to the Taj Trapezium Zone, for developing greenery to keep the air clean near the Taj Mahal,” he said, requesting anonymity.
Proposed in 2002, the Taj heritage corridor was an ambitious plan of then- CM Mayawati, under which the Yamuna would be diverted to reclaim about 75 acres of riverbed between the Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal for food plazas, shops and amusement facilities. But, environmentalists and a Supreme Court-appointed expert panel said the project was rushed through without ecological or structural studies and could endanger the two heritage sites. It was stayed by the Supreme Court in May 2003 and a CBI probe into irregularities in the project was ordered in July 2003. “Expert committees constituted on the instruction of the Supreme Court found that the best way to safeguard the reclaimed area was to develop greenery on the affected patches alongside the river Yamuna, and the Supreme Court approved the plan,” activist KC Jain said.
Also read: Floral patterned marble slab from Taj Mahal set for UK auction
In its landmark 1996 Taj Trapezium judgment, the Supreme Court noted that sulphur dioxide from nearby industries combined with moisture in the air to form sulphuric acid. In May 2018, a Supreme Court bench of justices MB Lokur and Deepak Gupta expressed concern that the Taj’s marble had turned yellowish, then brownish and greenish. Experts have long linked the loss of green cover to the Taj’s discolouration.
“The continuous felling of trees in the Taj Trapezium Zone, along with dust and vehicular pollution, is a significant contributor to the yellowing of the Taj Mahal’s marble,” said SN Tripathi of IIT Kanpur’s Centre for Environmental Science and Engineering.

morning.text:
Saubhadra Chatterji is Deputy Political Editor at the Hindustan Times. He writes on both politics and policies.
INDIA bloc races to consolidate Opposition against delimitation bill, may appeal to DMK
Some opposition parties have asked lawmakers to reach Delhi by Sunday, some are trying to protect MPs from possible poaching.
The beleaguered INDIA bloc has begun preparing for one last fight against the delimitation-related constitutional amendment bill, even as the odds appear increasingly stacked against it. Some opposition parties have asked lawmakers to reach Delhi by Sunday, some are trying to protect MPs from possible poaching while the INDIA bloc is considering making a public appeal to DMK chief MK Stalin on Saturday, indicated two senior opposition leaders.
The Congress’s strategy group met at 10, Janpath, and later announced it would continue to fight. Congress’s deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi told reporters, “The government is attempting to bring back the Delimitation Bill. Congress’ demand has been clear right from the beginning; we want the current strength in Lok Sabha should be upheld. Second, 33% women’s reservation should be done on the current strength. Third, the proportion of the strength of various states in Lok Sabha should be frozen for the coming 25 years. But on the pretext of women’s reservation, Prime Minister Modi and home minister Amit Shah want to do delimitation.”
The delimitation commission, by law, should have a member from the Election Commission of India, nominated by the Chief Election Commissioner. Gogoi flagged the issue and alleged that the government has tried to ensure “first, through manipulation of SIR and voter list to see who can vote and who cannot, now through delimitation where they can vote and where they cannot vote. This is all being done through the Election Commission...They have turned EC into a puppet and done injustice to people. Can we expect them to do justice as far as delimitation is concerned? Can we expect a party which is doing manipulation to be thinking of the welfare of the country? All they want to do is to change the Constitution one day. Congress will continue to fight”.
Opposition parties to hold meet
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal told the media, “PM Modi and Amit Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this entire episode. The INDIA alliance and opposition parties will have a meeting tomorrow morning at 11:30 AM. We will make the strategy.”
When asked if they are reaching out to the DMK, Venugopal said: “We are approaching everybody. The DMK always stands for the Constitution of India. I think whoever loves the Constitution of India cannot support these types of divisive agendas. So, we will approach all the opposition parties.”
The extension of the monsoon session (a special session) has been called from November 30 in the Lok Sabha and December 2 in the Upper House. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the sitting of both Houses would conclude on December 3.
Opposition to reach out to Stalin
CPI(M) chief MA Baby told HT, “We have asked our state leaders to talk to Stalin. They will talk to him to prevent the politicisation of the Thiruparankundram issue and try to persuade him not to support the delimitation bill.” Trinamool Congress’ Rajya Sabha floor leader Derek O’Brien, however, refuted reports that TMC chief Mamata Banerjee has spoken to Stalin but indicated that there is a possibility of the INDIA bloc making a public appeal to the former Tamil Nadu chief minister.
VCK chief Thol Thirumavalavan urged the DMK not to support the delimitation bill, saying the party was one of the main reasons the bill was defeated earlier and should not fail the people this time, given its long political legacy.
The parliament numbers game
In April, this year, the INDIA bloc mustered 230 votes (as against the minimum requirement of 181 votes) to defeat the 131st Constitution amendment bill. Now, the bloc stares at the possibility of depletion of at least 57 lawmakers in the Lok Sabha.
22 DMK and 20 rebel TMC MPs are set to support the bill. Six of the nine MPs of Sena (UBT) had joined Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena on June 22 and Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction has indicated its support for the upcoming delimitation bill. Trinamool Congress might suffer another setback as its senior MP, Kalyan Banerjee is facing suspension from the House for the remainder of the monsoon session. The party’s Lok Sabha floor leader Abhishek Banerjee has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on revoking Kalyan’s suspension.
In the strategy meeting, some leaders reported that not all DMK or NCP-SP MPs are in favour of the Delimitation and some of them might vote against the bill.
The sense of urgency has gripped the Opposition bloc. O’Brien said that all parties will issue three-line whips—making it mandatory for the MPs to vote against the bill. “Some parties have also asked their MPs to reach Delhi by Sunday,” he said. Another Opposition floor leader said that some MPs are being “protected” from possible poaching.
‘This is no way to deal with Opposition leaders’
O’Brien added that parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju called some Opposition leaders to inform that the government is bringing the delimitation-related bills. “I told him that we have already heard about it on X and that this is no way to deal with Opposition leaders.”
RJD chief Tejashwi Yadav told the media, “There is a difference between what is said and what is done. We will comment when it is implemented. The BJP has been in power in several places for years, but nothing has happened so far. It could be that these statements are being made keeping the elections in mind. You all are aware of our longstanding stand on women’s reservation. It would have been better if all parties had sat together and held discussions and consultations. Everyone knows our stand on the issue.”
Opposition leaders on Friday mounted a sharp pushback against the planned constitutional amendment bill to redraw parliamentary and assembly constituencies, with Congress communications chief Jairam Ramesh accusing the Modi government of trying to “manufacture a fraudulent two-thirds majority” in the Lok Sabha and pledging all-out resistance.
Also Read I NCP(SP) MLA says party backs delimitation bill, Sule clarifies final decision yet to be taken
In two posts before the party’s parliamentary strategy group meets later today to discuss the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, Ramesh accused the government of issuing misleading statements linking implementation of the women’s reservation law already passed in 2023 to its plans to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha.
“The Special Session is thus NOT for women’s reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years. The Special Session is for Delimitation. And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process,” the Congress leader said.

morning.text:
Smriti covers an intersection of politics and governance. Having spent over a decade in journalism, she combines old fashioned leg work with modern story telling tools.
Cabinet clears 50% Lok Sabha seat hike, freezes share till 2051
The legislation would also enable 33% women’s reservation after delimitation, potentially before the 2029 general election.
The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared two bills that increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in every state and Union Territory by 50%, raise the ceiling of the Lower House of Parliament to 850, and freeze the arrangement for the next 25 years, marking an ambitious agenda that can reshape India’s democracy for decades.
The 132nd Constitution Amendment Bill and the Delimitation (Second) Bill will also pave the way for implementing 33% reservation for women immediately after the delimitation exercise, set up delimitation commissions for the purpose, and effect a proportional rise of 50% in the strength of state assemblies, with a cap of 650 – relevant for Uttar Pradesh.
“The proposed bill would facilitate delimitation and put in operation the reservation of seats for women in the House of the people and the legislative assemblies. This will also promote women empowerment and provide opportunity for women to participate in the nation-building process and will facilitate inclusivity and help in achieving the goals of Viksit Bharat @ 2047,” said the statement of objects and reasons by Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal.
Deep Dive
Women's reservation to take effect after delimitation exercise
The seats reserved for women will be rotated in accordance to the delimitation commission’s order and be in place for 15 years. If the bills pass, it will make the Lok Sabha the world’s largest directly elected national legislative chamber.
A Constitution amendment bill will require two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha and 50% of all states to ratify. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) appears within striking distance of achieving this magic figure in both Houses, which are reconvening on Monday for a four-day special sitting.
In April, the government introduced the 131st Constitution Amendment bill and two other linked legislation to operationalise women’s reservation and implement delimitation. But the bill failed to garner the required majority in the face of united Opposition. It was the first time a Constitution amendment bill failed to get the required strength in the Lok Sabha since 2011, when a bill to give the Lokpal constitutional status was defeated.
Also read: Delimitation Bill proposes formation of commission, SC judge, CEC nominee among members
But since then, unprecedented churn in the Opposition ranks – rebellion within the Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) – as well as willingness from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) have indicated that the NDA might be more successful this time.
Delimitation has been an explosive issue in India since the 1970s when zooming populations and demographic differences first started causing anxieties.
The Constitution mandated regular delimitations after every census but the size of the Lok Sabha was frozen in 1971 in the face of protests from southern states, which argued that they shouldn’t be penalised for controlling their populations better than the northern states.
Under the new constitutional amendment bill, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha will rise to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories (it is 530 and 20 now, respectively), while the maximum strength of state legislative assemblies will increase to 650.
Also read: First time in 1952, a 1976 freeze: Tracing the journey of delimitation in India
Revised formula seeks to preserve states' relative representation
The proposed 50% expansion will apply to the existing allocation of seats in each state and Union Territory, thereby preserving their relative share in the Lok Sabha rather than redistributing representation according to population differences. In application, the number is likely to be between 816 and 824 for the Lok Sabha depending on how half-seats are rounded up.
“The objective of the present bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to the scheduled castes and the scheduled tribes, in the House of the people and the legislative assemblies of the states and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise, and for the said purpose, such delimitation shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats in the House of the people and the legislative assemblies of the states and Union territories, over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation,” the Constitution amendment bill said.
This will translate to women getting between 270 and 272 reserved seats in the Lower House if the bills are passed and the act comes into effect.
In its explanation for withdrawing the earlier legislation, the government acknowledged that concerns were expressed over the possible impact of delimitation on the representation of different states, particularly because of variations in population growth. It said the revised framework was intended to provide a more balanced arrangement while preserving the representative character of Parliament.
Also read: Govt’s delimitation plan: 50% seat hike for every state, Lok Sabha strength ceiling rises to 850
“The government has examined these issues with a view to ensuring that the constitutional framework for the next delimitation exercise is clear, balanced and capable of addressing the concerns raised while preserving the representative character,” said Meghwal in his statement for withdrawing the earlier delimitation bill.
The 132nd Constitution amendment bill noted that the strength of state assemblies will be increased by 50% of the current strength, subject to a cap of 650 seats. This cap was earlier 500.
“Such a uniform increase would enhance the overall representation of the people while maintaining the existing relative distribution of seats among the states,” Meghwal’s statement said.
The change is relevant for Uttar Pradesh, where the strength of the assembly is set to rise to over 600 from its current 403 if the bills pass in Parliament next week. The earlier cap of 500 could not have accommodated any proportional 50% rise in UP’s assembly seat strength.
The Constitution amendment bill also freezes the delimitation arrangement till 2051.
“In article 330 of the Constitution, in the proviso to the explanation, for the words and figures “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, be construed as a reference to the 2001 census”, the words, figures and brackets “until the year 2051, be construed as a reference to the latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026” shall be substituted,” the bill said.
The delimitation bill also provided for the constitution of a delimitation commission. At the national level, the body will comprise a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge appointed by the Centre as chairperson, the chief election commissioner (CEC) or an election commissioner nominated by the CEC, and the state election commissioner of the relevant state.
Also read: Centre’s delimitation plan: States’ proportionate Lok Sabha share to be frozen until 2051
Delimitation commission will be formed after the bill passes
The delimitation commission will be formed soon after Parliament passes the bill and the women’s bill will be implemented soon after the exercise is done, indicating that 33% women’s quota might be rolled out before the 2029 general elections.
The delimitation will be done on the basis “the latest census figures published as on the date of the commencement of this act” – which suggests the 2011 census.
“It shall be the duty of the commission to readjust,— (a) the allocation of seats in the House of the People to the states and Union territories and the total number of seats in the legislative assembly of each state, in accordance with the provisions of this act; and (b) the division of each state and Union territory into territorial constituencies, on the basis of the latest census figures, for the purpose,” the bill said.
In each state, the commission will have 10 people – five MPs and five MLAs, to be nominated by the speaker of the Lok Sabha and assembly respectively – as associate members. For those provinces where the number of MPs is five or less, all members will be associate members.
“The Election Commission shall act as delimitation commission for the purpose of delimiting constituencies in the legislative assembly of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir falling under the occupation of Pakistan, when the area of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the occupation of Pakistan ceases to be so occupied,” the bill said.
The state election commissioner appointed by the governor under Article 243K will be a member.
However, for two states, Meghalaya and Nagaland, a person nominated by the governor will act as the state election commissioner for this purpose. The Union Government will decide the period for which the commission will function through a notification, with an extension possible.

morning.title: Election Commission notifies new dates for special summary revision in Bengal
morning.text:
Election Commission notifies new dates for special summary revision in Bengal
Under the new timeline, rationalisation and rearrangement of polling stations will be completed by December 3.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday notified a revised schedule for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal, setting January 1, 2027 as the qualifying date and February 8 for publication of the final voter list, days after the state election office abruptly postponed the exercise.
Under the new timeline, rationalisation and rearrangement of polling stations will be completed by December 3 and the integrated draft electoral roll will be published on December 15. Voters will be able to file claims and objections from December 15 to January 14, 2027 which ECI will dispose of by February 1, the Commission said.
The January 1 qualifying date means those who turn 18 on or before that date will be eligible to enrol as voters.
Request from West Bengal CEO
The revision follows a request from the West Bengal chief electoral officer (CEO), which the Commission said it had accepted. “We received a request along with a proposed schedule from the West Bengal CEO’s office. The request was processed accordingly,” a senior ECI official, requesting anonymity, said. The state CEO declined to comment.
In its letter to the CEO, seen by HT, ECI said it had “acceded to the proposal” made by the state election office on November 18. It directed the state to give wide publicity to the revised schedule and inform political parties in writing.
Also Read I 10.39 lakh Form 6 applications during 7 days of SSR in UP
The SSR was originally scheduled to begin on November 23. On November 20, the CEO’s office announced that it “is hereby postponed due to some unavoidable circumstances”, without specifying the reason.
ECI had subsequently told HT that it was unaware of the reason for the postponement and that the decision had been taken by the state CEO’s office. The Commission on Friday also approved the state’s proposal to rationalise and shift polling stations. The proposal, sent through letters dated November 13, 14 and 20, will result in changes to polling-station locations, although ECI’s letter did not specify the stations affected.
“In this context, all the political parties shall be informed and wide publicity shall be done in the concerned polling areas to create awareness among voters about the new locations of the polling stations. All concerned officials may also be informed accordingly for necessary action,” ECI said in its letter.
SSR order in West Bengal
The SSR is a routine annual exercise that updates existing rolls by enrolling new and first-time voters, correcting personal details, shifting addresses and disposing of claims and objections. It is different from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which involves a much more extensive verification of existing voters. SIR involves door-to-door verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs), who distribute and collect enumeration forms. Voters who cannot be found or verified may be left out of the draft roll and can seek inclusion through claims and objections.
The revised SSR schedule comes against the backdrop of concerns over the ongoing electoral-roll revision in West Bengal.
HT reported on Thursday that several voters whose inclusion in the rolls was challenged by the CEO during the SIR were unable to track the status of their appeals on the ECINET portal. The issue has added to scrutiny of the adjudication process, which is handling millions of claims and appeals.
ECI had ordered the SSR on October 15 under Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, for 17 states and Union territories, including West Bengal. The schedule for states undergoing or having recently completed the SIR was to be announced separately. The SSR was stalled in these states while the ECI conducted the SIR. Draft rolls under the SSR were published on November 12 for 14 states, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with Uttar Pradesh’s following on November 17.
ECI has now asked states to use the SSR to clean up their rolls after the SIR. In a November 25 letter to CEOs of 25 states and UTs, including West Bengal, it directed officials to compare existing voter details with information collected during the SIR.
ECI stressed that all corrections will be made only through a Form-8 signed by the elector and subject to verification and approval. “No changes shall be made solely on the basis of automated identification”.
The TMC has repeatedly raised concerns over the exclusion of legitimate voters during the revision process. “All legitimate voters must be included in the voter’s list. Neither the draft list nor the final list can be published even if one legitimate voter is excluded. Elections have to be held based on that error-free voters’ list,” said Kunal Ghosh, TMC spokesperson.

morning.text:
New Delhi: Japan has announced that its Self-Defence Forces will begin using Indian firing ranges next year to test long-range missiles, following the conclusion of meetings between the foreign ministers and defence ministers of the two countries Thursday for the 2+2 Dialogue in Tokyo.
India has also raised its expectation for early consideration of the agreements related to co-production of the UNICORN (Unified Complex Radio) naval antenna. The first agreement on the co-production of UNICORN was announced earlier this year by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s visit to New Delhi in July.
The Joint Statement issued following the 2+2 Dialogue highlighted the expectation for Acceptance of Necessity for the UNICORN naval radio antenna by February 2027.
“This 2+2 meeting takes place at a time when the global order is being subjected to multiple shocks. There are two major ongoing conflicts whose impact have been felt even in distant regions. Coupled with the growing economic volatility and the after effects of the Covid pandemic, there are very strong concerns about energy, trade, food and health security. As we seek to secure ourselves on these fronts, trusted and substantive partnerships like ours become more valuable,” S. Jaishankar, India’s External Affairs Minister said in a statement to the press, following the 2+2 Dialogue.
He added, “Our 2+2 meeting naturally took into account the changing nature of warfare. We are witnessing the effective application of smart weapons and innovative solutions. Our cooperation here feeds into a larger engagement on innovation and startups. The big picture that our cooperation seeks to support is a multi-polar Asia and a multi-polar world.”
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted that he and his counterpart Shinjirō Koizumi “concurred” in moving forward to “swiftly realise concrete cooperation in fields of maritime and air domain awareness, search and rescue and information sharing agreements”.
He said, “We expressed our expectations for the early consideration of the UNICORN-related agreements and look forward to further strengthening our defence industrial cooperation under the framework of ‘Design with Japan and Make in India’.”
The Indian Defence Minister also highlighted the “need” for early conclusion of a maritime ship repair arrangement, which would allow for reciprocal provisions of ship repair facilities. Additionally, Singh underlined that niche technologies, underwater technologies and space domain awareness was also discussed. The two ministers agreed to “enhance” cooperation in anti-mine measures as well.
The major announcement of Japanese Self-Defence Forces using Indian testing ranges was made by Koizumi in a statement on X.
“We agreed that next year, the Self-Defense Forces will use an Indian firing range for the first time. This is also a major step strategically,” he wrote.

Last month, the Japanese Ground Self-Defence Force Chief of Staff General Masayoshi Arai had confirmed to local media that officials had been dispatched to India to inspect possible testing ranges for training with the Type-25 surface-to-ship missile. This missile has a range of roughly 1,000 kilometres.
“They welcomed the signing of LOI (Letter of Intent) toward the utilisation of firing ranges in India, whereby Japan Self-Defence Forces would, for the first time, conduct live-fire training etc., including those involving surface-to-ship missiles, at firing ranges in India,” Thursday’s Joint Statement read.
On Wednesday, Singh and Koizumi toured the Japanese Maritime Self-Defence Forces base at Yokosuka. Singh inspected the Mogami-class frigate JS Natori.
Jaishankar and Singh co-chaired the 2+2 Dialogue Thursday. The Indian External Affairs Minister reached Tokyo Wednesday, following his two-day visit to Manila alongside Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the India-ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) summit.
Singh and Koizumi have met three times in the last three months. They had met in New Delhi in August, and in Cebu, the Philippines last month on the margins of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus. The intensification of high-level meetings points to growing strategic convergences between New Delhi and Tokyo.
Jaishankar also held the India-Japan Foreign Ministers’ Strategic Dialogue during his visit to Tokyo, along with his Japanese counterpart Toshimitsu Motegi.
Apart from the 2+2 Dialogue, the two countries also launched a commemorative logo representing 75 years of the establishment of diplomatic ties, which will be celebrated in 2027.
Also Read: Trump pushes AI, military cooperation at Quad summit; India pushes safety of seafarers
China’s looming shadow
For Japan, India has increasingly become key to its strategic agenda as ties with China continue to remain tense. Japanese PM Takaichi travelled to China’s Shenzhen Wednesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, following her two-day visit to the Philippines for ASEAN-related summits.
However, China has sought to recast Japan’s recent military build-up as one that has potential to “destabilise Asia”, according to a report by The New York Times.
China and Japan have been in a war of words, especially after Takaichi announced that Japan may be forced to defend Taiwan—the self-governing territory, recognised by India as Chinese territory—in case of any future invasion by China.
Takaichi has moved to loosen export rules for military weapons, and increased defence spending to two percent of Japan’s gross domestic product (GDP) about two-years earlier than planned. In the looming shadow extended by Beijing, New Delhi has sought to describe its relationship with Tokyo as one that has an important role for stability across the Indo-Pacific.
“We also spoke about a growing tendency to weaponise connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares. Many of these have direct implications for our national security. Strengthening resilience and exploring new options must be seen in that context. Concerns about connectivity and chokepoints have grown in the light of experiences in the Gulf,” said Jaishankar in his remarks to the press.
“We are two significant nations of the Indo-Pacific with a long and continuous history of friendship and goodwill. As we enter an era where each nation has to step-up its contributions to the global order, a stronger India-Japan relationship can certainly play a more important role. Our 2+2 discussions today and the understanding we reached were a very good step in that direction.”
As the war of words between China and Japan intensified this year, Beijing has imposed a number of export restrictions on merchandise flowing to Tokyo, pointing to the “weaponisation” of resources and supply chains. One of the earliest export restrictions on rare earth elements (REEs) was imposed by China in 2010 on exports to Japan, following a boat collision in the disputed territory of Senkaku islands.
